title: Watermarking AI Outputs
summary: Attach or detect provenance signals in generated content while treating watermark evidence as limited, attack-sensitive, and distinct from proof of truth.
overview: AI-output watermarking embeds a detectable signal into generated content or associates it with provenance metadata. Text watermarking may influence token selection to create a statistical pattern; media systems may embed signals in pixels or audio. Signed provenance manifests are a related but distinct mechanism that records assertions about an asset's history.

No universal detector can reliably identify every AI-generated artifact. Editing, paraphrasing, translation, cropping, or recompression may weaken signals, and statistical tests can produce false positives. A watermark can indicate a particular generation process under stated assumptions; it does not establish factual accuracy, ownership, or the identity of every later editor.

production.poc: A prototype should test detection on both marked and unmarked content, including realistic transformations. Short text may provide too little evidence for confident detection.
production.production: Production defines the supported content types, generation path, detection thresholds, key custody, and user-facing interpretation. Preserve original artifacts and provenance records separately from transformed copies.
production.scale: At scale, version watermark algorithms and detector configurations, monitor false positives, and maintain compatibility with editing pipelines. Never use a weak detection signal as the sole basis for a consequential accusation.

components.name: Marking service
components.role: Applies the chosen signal during generation or asset publication where the format supports it.

components.name: Provenance record
components.role: Stores generation and editing assertions with appropriate signatures and asset bindings.

components.name: Key management
components.role: Protects watermark or signing keys and supports rotation and verification history.

components.name: Detection service
components.role: Evaluates candidate artifacts with calibrated thresholds and explicit uncertainty.

components.name: Transformation evaluator
components.role: Tests robustness under expected editing, compression, and redistribution workflows.

flow.title: Define evidence goal
flow.description: Decide whether the requirement is origin detection, tamper evidence, or visible disclosure.

flow.title: Apply signal
flow.description: Mark supported output through the approved generation or publication path.

flow.title: Bind provenance
flow.description: Associate the asset with versioned generation metadata and protected integrity evidence.

flow.title: Publish and transform
flow.description: Track how downstream editors and formats may preserve or remove the signal.

flow.title: Detect carefully
flow.description: Evaluate the artifact with the correct algorithm version and sufficient evidence length.

flow.title: Report limitations
flow.description: Present confidence and provenance validity without claiming truth or universal AI detection.

useCase.title: Tracking generated promotional assets
useCase.situation: A media team creates AI-assisted promotional images that pass through agencies, cropping tools, and content-management systems.
useCase.problem: Asset metadata can disappear during export, making it difficult to distinguish approved generated material from untracked copies.
useCase.requirement: The assistant must preserve useful origin information without claiming that every transformed image remains detectable.
useCase.architecture: The publication pipeline adds supported watermark signals and stores signed provenance for the original approved asset.
runtime: An editor exports a resized version; automated checks measure whether the expected signal and metadata survived.
A later audit compares the distributed image with the original record and reports available provenance with uncertainty.
useCase.failure: If cropping removes the detectable signal, the system reports insufficient watermark evidence rather than declaring the image human-created.
useCase.impact: Measure detection precision, robustness by transformation, provenance retention, and false-positive rates on unmarked assets.

tradeoffs.benefit: Some evidence may survive metadata removal.
tradeoffs.cost: Transformations can weaken detection and affect content quality.

tradeoffs.benefit: Tampering with recorded assertions becomes detectable.
tradeoffs.cost: Metadata can be stripped and trust depends on signer identity.
More marked artifacts yield inconclusive results.

failures.scenario: A short text is falsely classified as marked
failures.detection: Calibration shows weak statistical support at that length.
failures.recovery: Report inconclusive evidence and avoid consequential automated decisions.

failures.detection: Key-status checks invalidate trust in affected provenance.
failures.recovery: Revoke the key and preserve a documented verification history.

mistakes.mistake: Calling a watermark proof of factual accuracy
mistakes.fix: Separate origin evidence from content verification.

mistakes.mistake: Treating no detection as proof of human authorship
mistakes.fix: Report the limits of the detector and transformation history.

whenToUse: Content provenance is valuable to publishing workflows.
The generation path supports an evaluated marking method.
Users can understand uncertain detection results.
whenNotToUse: Universal reliable AI detection is the requirement.
The signal would be the sole basis for punishment.
Expected transformations destroy the evidence needed for detection.
checklist: Calibrate on marked and unmarked content.
